title: Coordinate multiple classifiers in shared decision requests and independent flywheel sessions
description: Use catalog classifier revisions and source-neutral item lists for live/replay sessions. Batch compatible classifiers in one decision request with scoped rubric/examples/questions and mapped outputs. Maintain independent heads, feedback and trigger/optimization state. Cache complete shared requests; count usage once. Connect catalog labels/explanations to optimization without future-label leakage. Existing arXiv worker is not completion of this general coordinator.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implemented classifier/item-list revisioned catalog, independent per-classifier item feedback and corrections, GraphQL API and navigation/labeling screens. Imported 250 saved arXiv articles through external chronological idempotent updater; no provider calls. Added native Jev classify_many transport with scoped rubric/examples/questions, mapped outputs and usage counted once. Remaining: general worker/coordinator, connecting catalog labels into learning, complete-request cache, attaching live/replay run configurations and migrating historical label provenance (do not silently reuse across new classifier revisions). No fresh optimization study executed.

comments.author: home

Real workspace idle at 175 completed/2 failed jobs, no labels or paid calls changed; server runtime deployment not yet restarted. Wider acceptance and Laya protocol/evaluation work remain open.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Fixed a cache isolation gap for custom Jev/Kev endpoints: the configured model identity now includes an opaque SHA-256 endpoint suffix. Default identities remain compatible; trailing slashes are equivalent, and URL details are not disclosed by the identity. Older custom-server cached answers remain stored but are not silently reused under the new identity. New adapter specs reproduced the collision before the fix; a real SharedDecisions SQLite spec with fake Kev transports verifies separate answers across servers and cache reuse when returning to the original server. Focused tests pass; full regression in progress. No production votes, paid calls, or server process changed.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Final verification for endpoint-aware cache identities: all 713 Python tests pass, including the cross-server durable joint-cache regression. No network or credentials used in the specs. Documentation records compatibility and safe cache-miss behavior for historical custom-server answers. Remaining scorecard/Laya/acceptance work remains open.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Found and reproduced a shared-request cache defect: prepared child answers survived later batch-scope changes, while the engine fingerprint used the most recent global batch identity. Added specs for scope changes, identity stability before/after execution, sibling-rubric changes, and engine-level solo/joint separation. Prepared children now belong only to the latest batch; the engine uses an optional request-specific cache_identity adapter hook. Durable complete-batch cache remains reusable; old ambiguous engine entries are not reused under shared-answer-v2 keys. Five shared-cache specs and 14 focused coordinator/cache specs pass; full regression running. This does not yet prove that numerical heads trained from solo feature requests transfer safely to joint inference: joint-context feature provenance and sibling-change head invalidation/refitting remain a required acceptance gap. Explicit refresh propagation through shared adapter also needs verification.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implemented pinned sibling context for candidate feature collection and inference. Heads now persist a stable feature-context identity (provider, classifier configs, and actual selected example records); context-aware adapters expose this through feature_context_identity. Changed sibling context invalidates only the head, preserving learned rubric/examples/questions. Workspace attempts bounded classifier refits inside the next item cycle, records shared-context-change triggers, and never serves an incompatible head. Round/stage/training caches include context identity. Specs verify candidate requests retain siblings, candidate answers cannot contaminate later baseline requests, stale-head invalidation preserves rubric, restart prediction rejects old context, and a real multi-wheel preparation refits before prediction within the same cycle. Focused specs pass; final full regression in progress. Production replay/objective comparisons and explicit shared refresh propagation remain unverified.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Final numerical/context regression: 731 Python specs pass after the bound-context candidate/baseline isolation fix. Added a clickable head-invalidated marker to the ML optimization lane; all 11 timeline/playback specs pass. The old head is never applied after a context change, even on restart, and its rubric remains intact. Complete final suite is running with the added timeline spec. No production labels or provider calls were changed by verification.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Completed shared cache option propagation. A refresh now recollects the entire joint provider request rather than returning the cached batch; durable per-request answer generations invalidate sibling outer caches. Previous batch responses/statuses remain in batch_history. Failed refresh cannot silently retry and explicit retry_failed reaches the underlying batch guard; physical request ceilings remain in force. Observer events expose generation, cache_policy, and retry_failed, and child exchanges expose shared_answer_generation. New fake-model specs reproduced the refresh bug, verify both sibling outputs update without extra calls, and verify failure history/explicit retry. Full regression: 734 Python specs and 102 UI tests pass; build and lint complete (existing lint warnings remain). Concurrent flat-interface changes are integrated in develop as 5a6a526. Remaining acceptance includes how explicit refresh of already-fitted training answers invalidates derived fitting/selection caches; do not claim that refresh alone recalculates all learned artifacts.
